flow: getReqAccessKeyV4 parses the SigV4 Credential access key and passes it to checkKeyValid
checkKeyValid resolves that exact key to auth.Credentials, preserving distinct AccessKey and ParentUser fields and validating any session token
validateAdminSignature returns the resolved signer credential
checkAdminRequestAuth authorizes admin:DeleteUser with AccountName equal to signer cred.AccessKey
validateAdminReq returns the same signer credential to RemoveUser
RemoveUser compares target accessKey with global root AccessKey and signer cred.AccessKey; it does not compare target with cred.ParentUser

derived_parent_consequence.statement: An STS signer access key differs from its ParentUser, so an STS signer that is granted admin:DeleteUser can target its parent without being classified as self.

existence_and_idempotency.explanation: The store-level deletion tolerates errNoSuchUser, but the handler's earlier IsTempUser precheck intercepts a later sequential request.

possible_results: 200 and 200 if both requests pass the unlocked handler prechecks before deletion

cascade_order: remove regular user from all persistent group memberships
scan iamUsersMap for credentials whose ParentUser equals the target
delete derived service accounts found by that scan; an STS switch branch is present but ordinary STS storage uses iamSTSAccountsMap
delete the target's mapped policy and evict iamUserPolicyMap
delete the target identity, tolerating errNoSuchUser at this internal layer
evict target caches and update cache.updatedAt
effects.regular_user: deleted from persistent identity storage and local cache
effects.mapped_user_policy: the user-to-policy mapping is deleted; canned policy documents remain
effects.groups: the user is removed from group memberships; group records and group policy mappings remain
effects.service_accounts: DeleteUser scans derived service accounts and attempts deletion; per-service-account deletion errors are ignored

sts_sessions.conclusion: ordinary STS persistence/revocation is not proven by this path
